evidence_chain.quote: Presentation: A 26-year-old female (primigravida) underwent an emergency cesarean section at 40 weeks after failed induction. The surgery was completed under spinal anesthesia, and a male neonate was delivered with a birthweight of 3.47 kg and a length of 51 cm. There were no complications during pregnancy, and all prenatal sonographic exams were normal. The newborn examination showed no dysmorphism. Post-C-section, the baby was transferred to the nursery for routine care and feeding. However, 24 hours post-delivery, the baby was moved to the neonatal intensive care unit due to poor feeding, bilious vomiting, and abdominal distension.

evidence_chain.quote: Most children with HD present during the neonatal period with delayed passage of meconium beyond the first 24 hours, abdominal distention, bilious vomiting and feeding intolerance and are diagnosed by a rectal biopsy in the first month of life.
